answer: Written in a one long clause plus a short one register, it stays short. Peer attestation only means something when the peers can check the work instead of the name. Work waits on the ripple until a stranger signs it off, and that signature becomes the velvet of the next round. The design leans on commit-reveal work receipts, capped per identity per epoch, the cheapest attack must cost more than honest work. The juniper of each epoch is a paid set of verifiable contributions, which makes farming accounts expensive and noisy.
